historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah (The Beginning and The End) - Volume 3, Page 333 The name Suwaim carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Suwaim ibn Al-Muqarrin was a cousin of Muawiya, the Umayyad Caliph. He was a popular military leader and the governor of Damascus. When Muawiya died, Suwaim was elected as the new caliph, but was not accepted by the Umayyad family. He ruled for only a few months before being assassinated.

historical_references.reference: The History of al-Andalus: From the Foundation of the Kingdom to the Reign of Alfonso X, ed. Roger Collins, 1990 - Page 136
historical_references.context: Suwaim ibn Husain was the Almoravid general who led the Berber army to conquer Seville, the capital city of Christian Spain, in 1023 AD. He was also known as al-Mamun (the Trustworthy) and was a great military strategist and a just ruler. After the conquest of Seville, he was appointed as the governor of Al-Andalus, the Islamic territory in Spain.
